notes:
1. V.O. Chidambaranar — Overview

  • V.O. Chidambaranar was a lawyer, entrepreneur, labour leader, Tamil scholar and freedom fighter.
  • He became one of the strongest leaders of the Swadeshi Movement in southern Tamil Nadu.
  • His greatest nationalist achievement was the establishment of the Swadeshi Steam Navigation Company to challenge British maritime monopoly.
  • He also played a pioneering role in organised labour agitation at Tuticorin.
📌 Must-Memorise

V.O.C. → Swadeshi Shipping + Tuticorin + Coral Mill Strike

2. Popular Name

  • V.O. Chidambaranar is popularly known as Kappalottiya Tamizhan, meaning the Tamil who sailed ships or Tamil Helmsman.
📌 Must-Memorise

Kappalottiya Tamizhan → V.O. Chidambaranar

3. Another Honorific

  • He is also remembered as Sekkizuththa Semmal or Chekkilutha Chemmal because of the brutal oil-press labour imposed on him in prison.
📌 Must-Memorise

Chekkilutha Chemmal → V.O.C. → Prison Oil Press

4. Birth

  • V.O.C. was born on 5 September 1872.
📌 Must-Memorise

V.O.C. → 5 September 1872

5. Birthplace

  • He was born at Ottapidaram in the Tirunelveli region of the Madras Presidency.
  • Ottapidaram is now in Thoothukudi district of Tamil Nadu.
📌 Must-Memorise

V.O.C. → Ottapidaram

6. Father

  • His father was Olaganathan Pillai.
  • He was a lawyer.
📌 Must-Memorise

V.O.C.'s Father → Olaganathan Pillai

7. Mother

  • His mother was Paramayee Ammal.
📌 Must-Memorise

Mother → Paramayee Ammal

8. Educational Background

  • V.O.C. studied in the Tirunelveli–Tuticorin region.
  • He studied at Caldwell College in Tuticorin according to the Government of India's biographical account.

9. Early Employment

  • Before entering legal practice, V.O.C. briefly worked as a taluk office clerk.

10. Legal Career

  • V.O.C. studied law and became a successful pleader.
  • Law provided him with:
  • Professional status.
  • Public contact.
  • Knowledge of colonial administration.

11. Move to Tuticorin

  • Tuticorin became the principal centre of V.O.C.'s legal, nationalist, commercial and labour activities.
  • He moved his professional focus there around the beginning of the twentieth century.
📌 Tamil Nadu Must-Memorise

V.O.C. → Tuticorin / Thoothukudi

12. Thoothukudi's Importance

  • Tuticorin was one of the major ports of the Madras Presidency.
  • It had important commercial connections with Ceylon, present-day Sri Lanka.

13. Political Entry

  • V.O.C. entered active nationalist politics around 1905.
  • The Partition of Bengal and the Swadeshi Movement provided the immediate national background.
📌 Must-Memorise

V.O.C. → Active Politics → 1905

14. Partition of Bengal

  • Lord Curzon partitioned Bengal in 1905.
  • The decision stimulated the Swadeshi and Boycott movements throughout India.

15. Swadeshi Idea

Swadeshi called for:

  • Use of indigenous goods.
  • Boycott of foreign goods.
  • Indian enterprise.
  • Economic self-reliance.

V.O.C. transformed this principle into a direct maritime business challenge to British power.

16. Bal Gangadhar Tilak

  • V.O.C. was strongly influenced by the assertive nationalist politics associated with Bal Gangadhar Tilak.
📌 Must-Memorise

V.O.C. → Tilak's Assertive Nationalist Influence

17. Lala Lajpat Rai

  • The broader nationalist ideas of leaders such as Lala Lajpat Rai also formed part of the Swadeshi environment that influenced V.O.C.

18. Lal-Bal-Pal Phase

  • V.O.C.'s rise belongs to the same wider phase of assertive nationalism associated with:
  • Lala Lajpat Rai.
  • Bal Gangadhar Tilak.
  • Bipin Chandra Pal.

19. Subramania Bharathiar

  • V.O.C. developed close nationalist links with Mahakavi Subramania Bharathiar.
📌 Tamil Nadu Must-Memorise

V.O.C. + Bharathiar → Tamil Swadeshi Nationalism

20. Subramania Siva

  • Subramania Siva became one of V.O.C.'s closest associates in the militant Swadeshi movement of southern Tamil Nadu.
📌 Must-Memorise

V.O.C. + Subramania Siva → Tuticorin–Tirunelveli Nationalism

21. Tamil Swadeshi Trio

For rapid memory:

  • V.O.C. → Economic/Shipping Swadeshi.
  • Bharathiar → Poetry and Journalism.
  • Subramania Siva → Fiery Public Oratory.
🔗 Tamil Nadu Key Link

V.O.C. + Bharathi + Siva → Southern Tamil Swadeshi Movement

22. Ramakrishna Mission Influence

  • V.O.C. also came into contact with the intellectual and spiritual environment associated with the Ramakrishna Mission.

23. Mandayam Family

  • The Mandayam nationalist circle in Madras was another link between V.O.C. and the wider Swadeshi movement.

24. British Shipping Monopoly

  • Passenger and cargo services between Tuticorin and Colombo were dominated by European companies.
  • The British India Steam Navigation Company was the principal competitor faced by V.O.C.'s Swadeshi venture.
📌 Must-Memorise

British Rival of V.O.C. → British India Steam Navigation Company

25. BISNCo

BISNCo → British India Steam Navigation Company.

⚠️ TNPSC Trap

SSNCo → Indian Swadeshi Company

BISNCo → British Rival

26. Tuticorin–Colombo Route

  • The key maritime route connected:
  • Tuticorin.
  • Colombo in Ceylon.
📌 Must-Memorise

V.O.C. Shipping Route → Tuticorin ↔ Colombo

27. Economic Nationalism

  • V.O.C. understood that political freedom required the weakening of British economic monopolies.
  • His shipping enterprise therefore combined:
  • Business.
  • Swadeshi.
  • Nationalism.

28. Swadeshi Steam Navigation Company

  • V.O.C. established the Swadeshi Steam Navigation Company in 1906.
📌 Must-Memorise

Swadeshi Steam Navigation Company → V.O.C. → 1906

29. Formal Registration

  • The company was formally established on 16 October 1906.
📌 Must-Memorise

SSNC → 16 October 1906

30. Headquarters

  • Tuticorin served as the home port and operational centre of the Swadeshi shipping enterprise.

31. Purpose of SSNC

Its goals included:

  • Challenging British monopoly.
  • Promoting Indian commerce.
  • Encouraging indigenous shipping.
  • Demonstrating economic self-reliance.

32. Capital

  • The company was organised through share capital subscribed by Indian supporters.
  • Nationalists, merchants and commercial groups were mobilised to finance the enterprise.

33. Nationalist Shareholding

  • The enterprise was designed not merely for private profit.
  • Purchasing shares itself became an expression of Swadeshi commitment.

34. Fundraising

  • V.O.C. travelled extensively to raise capital for the company.

35. Pandithurai Thevar

  • Pandithurai Thevar, associated with the Madurai Tamil Sangam, supported the Swadeshi Steam Navigation Company and held an important position in the enterprise.
🔗 Tamil Nadu Key Link

Pandithurai Thevar → Supporter of V.O.C.'s Shipping Venture

36. Haji Pakkir Mohammed Rowther

  • Muslim merchant support was also important to the company.
  • Haji Pakkir Mohammed Rowther was among the major investors associated with the enterprise.
🔗 TNPSC Key Link

SSNC → Cross-Community Indian Commercial Support

37. Swadeshi and Communal Unity

  • The company's supporter network included Indians of different communities.
  • Economic nationalism therefore provided a common anti-colonial platform.

38. Initial Difficulty

  • The company initially lacked its own vessels and depended on leased ships.

39. British Pressure

  • The British India Steam Navigation Company used its commercial influence to make it difficult for the Swadeshi company to obtain vessels and business.

40. Need for Own Ships

  • V.O.C. recognised that the company would survive only if it possessed vessels of its own.

41. S.S. Gallia

  • One of the principal ships acquired for the Swadeshi Steam Navigation Company was S.S. Gallia.
📌 Must-Memorise

SSNC Ship → S.S. Gallia

42. S.S. Lavo

  • The other famous vessel associated with the company was S.S. Lavo.
📌 Must-Memorise

SSNC Ships → Gallia + Lavo

43. Ships Purchased from Europe

  • The vessels were obtained from European sources, but their operation under an Indian-controlled Swadeshi company had enormous nationalist significance.

44. Bharathiar and Swadeshi Shipping

  • Subramania Bharathiar used nationalist journalism to promote Swadeshi economic initiatives such as V.O.C.'s shipping enterprise.

45. Shipping as National Symbol

The ships represented:

  • Indian entrepreneurship.
  • Resistance to monopoly.
  • Economic independence.
  • National pride.

46. Fare War

  • British shipping interests cut passenger fares in an effort to destroy the Swadeshi company's business.
  • V.O.C.'s company responded by lowering its own fares.
🔗 TNPSC Key Link

SSNC vs BISNCo → Fare War

47. Unequal Competition

  • BISNCo possessed:
  • Greater capital.
  • Established infrastructure.
  • Colonial administrative support.
  • SSNC depended heavily on nationalist public support.

48. British Administrative Pressure

  • Colonial officials subjected the Swadeshi enterprise to administrative and commercial pressure.
  • Its success was seen as politically dangerous.

49. Why SSNC Was Political

  • Every Indian passenger choosing the Swadeshi vessel over the British vessel could be seen as participating in economic boycott.

50. Nationalist Entrepreneurship

🔗 TNPSC Key Concept

V.O.C. transformed Swadeshi from:

Boycott of British Goods

into:

Creation of an Indian-Owned Alternative

51. Tirunelveli Nationalism

  • The shipping agitation helped transform Tirunelveli district into a major centre of assertive nationalist politics.

52. Swadeshi Sangam

  • Lawyers and activists supporting V.O.C. and Subramania Siva formed nationalist networks described as Swadeshi Sangam or National Volunteers.

53. Public Speeches

  • V.O.C. and Subramania Siva addressed large public meetings.
  • Their speeches linked:
  • Swadeshi.
  • Swaraj.
  • Economic resistance.

54. V.O.C. as Orator

  • V.O.C. became an effective Tamil political speaker.
  • He helped translate all-India nationalist ideas into a language accessible to local people.

55. Swadeshi Beyond Elites

  • The movement in Tuticorin began to attract:
  • Merchants.
  • Workers.
  • Lawyers.
  • Ordinary townspeople.

56. Labour Dimension

  • V.O.C.'s nationalism became particularly significant when he supported industrial workers at the Coral Mill.
📌 Must-Memorise

V.O.C. → Early Nationalist Labour Leadership

57. Coral Mill

  • Coral Mill was a British-owned textile mill at Tuticorin.
  • Working conditions were harsh.
📌 Must-Memorise

Coral Mill → Tuticorin

58. Working Conditions

Workers faced conditions involving:

  • Long hours.
  • Low wages.
  • Limited leave.
  • Strict industrial discipline.

59. Child and Young Labour

  • The Government of India's biographical account records a substantial young workforce in the mill, highlighting the harsh social character of colonial industrial employment.

60. Coral Mill Strike

  • The workers went on strike on 27 February 1908.
📌 Must-Memorise

Coral Mill Strike → 27 February 1908

61. Strike Leadership

  • V.O.C. and Subramania Siva actively supported the striking workers.
📌 Must-Memorise

Coral Mill → V.O.C. + Subramania Siva

62. Workers' Demands

Important demands included:

  • Higher wages.
  • Reduction in working hours.
  • Improved working conditions.

63. Weekly Holiday

  • Improved leave and rest provisions were among the labour issues raised during the strike.

64. Public Support

  • Residents of Tuticorin rallied behind the workers.
  • The strike therefore acquired both:
  • Labour character.
  • Nationalist character.

65. Strike Outcome

  • Management ultimately conceded important worker demands, including improvements in wages and working conditions.

66. Length of Strike

  • The strike lasted for approximately nine days before workers returned after concessions.

67. Historical Importance

  • The Coral Mill agitation was one of the important early examples of linking labour grievances with Indian nationalism.

68. Before Gandhi's Champaran

  • The Government of India explicitly notes that V.O.C.'s labour mobilisation preceded Gandhi's Champaran Satyagraha and marked him as an early working-class nationalist organiser.
🔗 TNPSC Key Link

V.O.C. Labour Movement → Before Gandhian Mass Leadership in India

69. Nationalism and Labour

V.O.C. demonstrated that Swaraj was connected with:

  • Political rights.
  • Economic freedom.
  • Workers' welfare.

70. Bipin Chandra Pal

  • In March 1908, nationalists planned celebrations connected with the release of Bipin Chandra Pal from prison.

71. Swaraj Day

  • V.O.C., Subramania Siva and other activists sought to hold public demonstrations celebrating nationalist resistance and Swaraj.

72. Padmanabha Iyengar

  • Padmanabha Iyengar was another important associate involved with V.O.C. and Subramania Siva in the Tirunelveli nationalist agitation.
📌 Must-Memorise

V.O.C. + Siva + Padmanabha Iyengar → 1908 Tirunelveli Agitation

73. Collector Wynch

  • District Collector Wynch sought to restrict nationalist meetings and activities.

74. British Fear

  • Colonial officials regarded the combination of:
  • Shipping Swadeshi.
  • Worker mobilisation.
  • Political speeches.

as a serious challenge to authority.

75. Arrest

  • V.O.C., Subramania Siva and Padmanabha Iyengar were arrested on 12 March 1908.
📌 Must-Memorise

V.O.C. Arrest → 12 March 1908

76. Immediate Reaction

  • Their arrest triggered widespread public anger in Tirunelveli and Tuticorin.

77. Tirunelveli Uprising

  • Demonstrations after the arrests developed into violent disturbances in Tirunelveli.
📌 Tamil Nadu Must-Memorise

1908 Tirunelveli Uprising → Arrest of V.O.C. and Siva

78. Closure of Institutions

  • Shops, educational institutions and public activity were disrupted as protests spread.

79. Government Buildings

  • During the unrest, colonial and municipal buildings became targets of attack.

80. Police Firing

  • Police firing during the disturbances caused deaths.

81. Tuticorin Protest

  • Workers and residents in Tuticorin also reacted strongly to the detention of nationalist leaders.

82. Political Strike

  • The response at Tuticorin has been described as an early political strike, showing how labour action had become connected to nationalist politics.

83. Sedition Charges

  • The colonial government prosecuted V.O.C. for sedition-related offences arising from his speeches and nationalist activities.
📌 Must-Memorise

V.O.C. → Sedition Case → 1908

84. Subramania Siva Charge

  • V.O.C. was also prosecuted in connection with his association with and support for Subramania Siva.

85. Sessions Court

  • The case was heard before the Sessions Court.
  • Judge A.F. Pinhey imposed an exceptionally severe sentence.
📌 Must-Memorise

V.O.C. Case → Judge Pinhey

86. Original Sentence

  • V.O.C. initially received two transportation-for-life sentences in the sedition proceedings.
📌 Must-Memorise

V.O.C. → Initially Two Life Sentences

87. Public Shock

  • The severity of the sentence produced widespread criticism.
  • Nationalist opinion regarded it as evidence of colonial repression.

88. Appeal

  • V.O.C. appealed to the Madras High Court.
  • His punishment was substantially reduced.

89. Reduced Sentence

  • The High Court reduced the punishment to shorter concurrent terms of transportation/imprisonment.
⚠️ TNPSC Caution

Original Sentence → Extremely Severe

Final Imprisonment → Reduced on Appeal

90. Rigorous Imprisonment

  • V.O.C. underwent rigorous imprisonment.

91. Palayamkottai Jail

  • He was initially confined in the southern prison system before being transferred.

92. Coimbatore Central Prison

  • V.O.C. was imprisoned at Coimbatore Central Prison.
📌 Must-Memorise

V.O.C. → Coimbatore Central Prison

93. Prison Hardship

  • Prison authorities subjected him to harsh manual labour despite his professional background as a lawyer.

94. Jute Machine

  • One of his prison assignments involved operating a jute-processing machine manually.
  • His hands became badly injured.

95. Oil Press

  • He was then forced to operate an oil press traditionally driven by animals.
📌 Must-Memorise

V.O.C. → Pulled Oil Press in Prison

96. Chekkilutha Chemmal

  • His suffering at the oil press gave rise to the enduring Tamil honorific Chekkilutha Chemmal.

97. Nationalist Symbolism

The image of V.O.C. at the oil press became a symbol of:

  • Colonial cruelty.
  • Personal sacrifice.
  • Tamil participation in the national struggle.

98. Coimbatore Prison Memorial

  • The Tamil Nadu Prison Department preserves the historical association of V.O.C. with Coimbatore Central Prison.

99. Kannur Prison

  • V.O.C. also spent part of his imprisonment in the prison system outside Tamil Nadu before his eventual release.

100. Release

  • V.O.C. was finally released from prison on 24 December 1912.
📌 Must-Memorise

V.O.C. Released → 24 December 1912

101. Years in Prison

  • His years of imprisonment severely damaged:
  • His health.
  • His legal career.
  • His financial position.

102. Legal Licence

  • His right to practise law was affected following his conviction.
  • He had to struggle to rebuild his professional life after release.

103. Financial Ruin

  • V.O.C. emerged from prison economically weakened.
  • The prosperous lawyer and businessman lived through serious financial hardship in later years.

104. Fate of Swadeshi Steam Navigation Company

  • Colonial pressure, commercial competition and the removal of its strongest nationalist leadership severely damaged the company.
  • The enterprise ultimately ceased operations and was liquidated in the early 1910s.

105. Company Liquidation

  • The Swadeshi Steam Navigation Company was liquidated in 1911.
📌 Must-Memorise

SSNC → 1906–1911

106. Historical Failure vs National Success

  • Commercially, the company did not survive.
  • Politically, it demonstrated that Indians could directly challenge a European monopoly.
🔗 TNPSC Key Link

SSNC → Commercially Defeated, Nationalistically Symbolic

107. British Economic Power

  • The company's experience demonstrated how colonial business enjoyed advantages unavailable to Indian competitors.

108. Economic Nationalism Lesson

V.O.C.'s strategy showed that nationalism could operate through:

  • Production.
  • Trade.
  • Transport.
  • Investment.
  • Consumer choice.

109. Robert Ashe

  • Robert William d'Escourt Ashe was a British district official associated with the suppression of the Swadeshi movement in the Tirunelveli region.

110. Ashe Assassination

  • Ashe was assassinated by Vanchinathan at Maniyachi railway station on 17 June 1911.
📌 Must-Memorise

Vanchinathan → Ashe → Maniyachi → 17 June 1911

111. SSNC Connection

  • During later proceedings, revolutionary anger against Ashe was linked partly to his role in suppressing nationalist activity and the Swadeshi shipping enterprise.

112. V.O.C. vs Vanchinathan

⚠️ TNPSC Trap

V.O.C.:

  • Swadeshi entrepreneur.
  • Labour leader.
  • Congress nationalist.

Vanchinathan:

  • Revolutionary who assassinated Ashe.

They were not the same type of nationalist activist.

113. Subramania Siva After 1908

  • Subramania Siva also suffered repeated imprisonment and severe hardship for nationalist activities.

114. Bharathiar After 1908

  • Bharathiar later moved to French Pondicherry, where he continued nationalist journalism and writing.

115. Tamil Swadeshi Suppression

By 1908–11, British repression had severely disrupted the network involving:

  • V.O.C.
  • Subramania Siva.
  • Bharathiar.
  • Other southern activists.

116. Return to Public Life

  • Despite poverty, V.O.C. continued to maintain nationalist interests after his release.

117. Gandhi Correspondence

  • Correspondence survives between Gandhi and V.O.C. from the mid-1910s.
🔗 TNPSC Key Link

V.O.C. → Pre-Gandhian Swadeshi Leader Who Later Corresponded with Gandhi

118. Gandhi Era

  • Gandhi became the dominant national leader after V.O.C.'s principal Swadeshi phase.
  • V.O.C.'s most celebrated political actions therefore predated:
  • Champaran.
  • Non-Cooperation.
  • Dandi.
⚠️ TNPSC Trap

V.O.C.'s Major Struggle → Before Gandhian Mass Era

119. Congress Differences

  • V.O.C.'s later relationship with Congress politics was not as dominant as his 1905–08 role.
  • He retained a strong independent nationalist personality.

120. Tilak Connection

  • V.O.C. remained particularly identified with the assertive nationalist tradition associated with Tilak.
📌 Must-Memorise

Tilak ↔ V.O.C. → Assertive Nationalism

121. Labour Leader

  • V.O.C.'s Coral Mill role gives him a special place in the history of the labour movement in Tamil Nadu.

122. Labour + Nationalism

🔗 TNPSC Key Concept

V.O.C. linked:

Worker Rights

  • Swadeshi
  • Swaraj

123. Maritime Nationalism

  • His shipping venture similarly linked:
  • Economic enterprise.
  • Anti-imperialism.
  • Indigenous control of transport.

124. Tamil Scholar

  • V.O.C. was also an important Tamil scholar and writer.
📌 Must-Memorise

V.O.C. → Freedom Fighter + Tamil Scholar

125. Autobiography

  • V.O.C. wrote an autobiography in Tamil verse.
  • He began the work in prison and completed it after release.
📌 Must-Memorise

V.O.C. → Tamil Verse Autobiography

126. Thirukkural

  • He wrote scholarly commentary connected with the Thirukkural.
🔗 Tamil Nadu Key Link

V.O.C. → Thirukkural Scholarship

127. Tolkappiyam

  • V.O.C. also worked with ancient Tamil grammatical literature including Tolkappiyam.

128. Meyyaram

  • Meyyaram is an important work associated with V.O.C.
📌 Must-Memorise

Meyyaram → V.O.C.

129. Meyyarivu

  • Meyyarivu is another important work associated with him.
📌 Must-Memorise

Meyyarivu → V.O.C.

130. James Allen

  • V.O.C. translated works of English writer James Allen into Tamil.
🔗 TNPSC Key Link

V.O.C. → Tamil Translator of James Allen

131. Literary Range

His writings included:

  • Ethics.
  • Philosophy.
  • Tamil classics.
  • Translation.
  • Autobiographical writing.

132. Scholar and Activist

  • V.O.C.'s importance therefore extends beyond shipping and politics to Tamil intellectual history.

133. Final Years

  • His later years were marked by financial difficulty.
  • He spent part of the 1930s in places including Kovilpatti before returning to Tuticorin.

134. Poverty

  • The Government of India's biographical account records that he lived under severe financial strain and even sold books to meet expenses.

135. Death

  • V.O. Chidambaranar died on 18 November 1936.
📌 Must-Memorise

V.O.C. → Died 18 November 1936

136. Place of Death

  • He died at Tuticorin.
📌 Must-Memorise

V.O.C. → Birth: Ottapidaram

Death: Tuticorin

137. Age

  • He was 64 years old when he died.

138. Independence

  • V.O.C. died more than a decade before India attained independence in 1947.

139. V.O. Chidambaranar Port

  • Tuticorin's major port now bears the name V.O. Chidambaranar Port, preserving his maritime nationalist legacy.
📌 Must-Memorise

Thoothukudi Port → Named for V.O. Chidambaranar

140. Why Port Naming Is Significant

  • The honour is especially appropriate because Tuticorin was the home port from which V.O.C. challenged British shipping domination.

141. V.O.C. Port Historical Memory

  • The official port history recognises V.O.C.'s role in sowing nationalism through Swadeshi and boycott of British shipping.

142. Birth Anniversary

  • 5 September is commemorated as the birth anniversary of V.O. Chidambaranar in Tamil Nadu.

143. V.O.C. Memorials

  • Tamil Nadu preserves several sites and memorials associated with:
  • Ottapidaram.
  • Tuticorin.
  • Coimbatore prison.

144. Nationalist Identity

V.O.C. can be remembered through three identities:

  • Kappalottiya Tamizhan → Shipping.
  • Labour leader → Coral Mill.
  • Chekkilutha Chemmal → Prison suffering.

145. Economic Contribution

His principal economic-nationalist contribution was:

  • Creation of indigenous maritime competition against a British monopoly.

146. Political Contribution

His political contribution was:

  • Making the Tirunelveli–Tuticorin region a major centre of assertive Swadeshi nationalism.

147. Labour Contribution

His labour contribution was:

  • Supporting the Coral Mill workers' strike and linking workplace demands with nationalism.

148. Cultural Contribution

His cultural contribution included:

  • Tamil writing.
  • Commentary.
  • Translation.
  • Study of classical works.

149. V.O.C. and Self-Reliance

  • His shipping company was an early practical demonstration of what would later be described as economic self-reliance.

150. Swadeshi Steam Navigation vs Boycott

Boycott alone:

  • Reject British service.

V.O.C.'s strategy:

  • Reject British service.
  • Create Indian service.
🔗 TNPSC Key Concept

V.O.C. → Constructive Economic Swadeshi

151. V.O.C. vs Dadabhai Naoroji

Dadabhai:

  • Analysed colonial economic exploitation through Drain Theory.

V.O.C.:

  • Challenged colonial economic power through Indian enterprise.

152. V.O.C. vs Tilak

Tilak:

  • Assertive all-India nationalist leader.

V.O.C.:

  • Southern Tamil leader influenced by the assertive nationalist current.

153. V.O.C. vs Gandhi

V.O.C.:

  • Major Swadeshi activity → 1905–08.

Gandhi:

  • Dominant Indian mass leadership → after 1915.
⚠️ TNPSC Trap

V.O.C.'s Coral Mill Strike Preceded Gandhi's Champaran

V.O.C.:

  • Swadeshi Steam Navigation.
  • Tuticorin.
  • 1906.

Rajaji:

  • Vedaranyam Salt Satyagraha.

1906 → V.O.C. → Shipping

V.O.C.:

  • Entrepreneur and labour organiser.

Bharathiar:

  • Poet and journalist.

Both:

  • Swadeshi nationalism.

156. V.O.C. vs Subramania Siva

V.O.C.:

  • Lawyer and entrepreneur.

Subramania Siva:

  • Fiery nationalist speaker.

Both:

  • Arrested during the 1908 agitation.

157. V.O.C. vs Vanchinathan

V.O.C.:

  • Economic and mass nationalist action.

Vanchinathan:

  • Revolutionary assassination of Ashe.

158. Key Organisations

  • Indian National Congress.
  • Swadeshi Steam Navigation Company.
  • Swadeshi/National Volunteer networks in Tirunelveli.

159. Key Places

  • Ottapidaram → Birth.
  • Tuticorin → Law, shipping, labour.
  • Colombo → Shipping route.
  • Tirunelveli → 1908 uprising.

  • Maniyachi → Ashe assassination.

  • Olaganathan Pillai → Father.
  • Paramayee Ammal → Mother.

  • Bharathiar → Nationalist associate.

  • Year → 1906.
